summary: Explains that handlers need names to be notified, or can use `listen` to subscribe to a topic so one notify triggers a group of handlers. `listen` decouples handlers from names for sharing across roles; duplicate handler names shadow earlier ones, with only the last loaded used.
questions: How do I trigger several handlers with one notify?
What does listen do on a handler?
What happens if two handlers have the same name?
How can I share handlers between roles without relying on their names?

answer_card.title: Handler names and listen topics
answer_card.answer_md:
Handlers must have a `name` to be notified, or can use `listen` to subscribe to a topic:

```yaml
tasks:
  - command: echo "restart web services"
    notify: "restart web services"
handlers:
  - name: Restart memcached
    service: {name: memcached, state: restarted}
    listen: "restart web services"
  - name: Restart apache
    service: {name: apache, state: restarted}
    listen: "restart web services"
```
Notifying the topic runs every handler listening to it, regardless of names. This makes it easier to share handlers across playbooks and roles.

Give each handler a globally unique name: with duplicates, only the last one loaded into the play can be notified and run.
